title: MDN — common image file types: JPEG/PNG/GIF/BMP/ICO/SVG universal; WebP Safari 14+; AVIF Chrome 85/Firefox 93/Safari 16.1+ (Firefox 93–112 stills only)
HTML Living Standard — drawing animated images to canvas uses the animation's default image / first frame (verbatim rule quoted)

MDN toBlob — 'if the given format is not supported, then the data will be exported as image/png' (Safari WebP silent fallback confirmed still true 2026 via MDN browser-compat-data HTMLCanvasElement.json: toBlob/toDataURL/convertToBlob image/webp Safari false); quality param 0–1 for lossy types; AVIF encode absent from all enumerations (inference flagged)
MDN browser-compat-data — OffscreenCanvas + convertToBlob: Chrome/Edge 69, Firefox 105, Safari/iOS 16.4+

MDN image-orientation — initial value from-image, Baseline since April 2020; createImageBitmap default also from-image (literal 'from-image' string only Chrome 112/Firefox 111/Safari 16+; older browsers apply default behavior but reject the string → omit the option)

MDN bcd — createImageBitmap resizeQuality ('high' explicit) Chrome 54/Safari 15/Firefox 149 (weeks old, implementation-defined); CanvasRenderingContext2D.imageSmoothingQuality: Firefox false → one-pass drawImage quality is cross-browser-inconsistent; progressive halving is the community-technique answer (no primary spec, flagged); pica v10.0.3 (Lanczos/mks2013 in workers, disables its createImageBitmap path as 'buggy in Chrome') held in backlog

canvas-size measured results (community-measured, flagged — no vendor docs exist): iOS area cap 16,777,216 px with 4096 px/side practical; desktop Chrome 65,535/side, 268M area; failures silent (toBlob → null, toDataURL → 'data:,')

client-zip v2.5.0 (2025-03-14, repo pushed 2026-06) — MIT, ~2.6 KB gzipped; exports downloadZip(files, options?) → Response, makeZip → ReadableStream, predictLength; inputs { name, lastModified, input } where input is Blob/Uint8Array/Response/File; STORE-only (no compression — correct for already-compressed PNGs)
MDN toBlob quality parameter compat — Chrome 50, Firefox 25, Safari 11; out-of-range/absent → browser default; PNG unaffected
MDN Blob.size — read-only byte count, baseline since 2015; basis of the before/after savings display (encode first, then report)

web.dev (Chrome team) install criteria — verbatim: 'icons - must include a 192px and a 512px icon'; plus MDN manifest icons reference (src/sizes 'WxH'/type/purpose any|maskable|monospace, 'specifying type can significantly improve performance'). The 36/48/72/96/144 ladder appears in no current Google documentation

ICO file format — ICONDIR (6 B: reserved=0, type=1, count) + ICONDIRENTRY (16 B each: bWidth/bHeight bytes where 0=256, bColorCount, bReserved, wPlanes 0-or-1, wBitCount, dwBytesInRes, dwImageOffset; little-endian); PNG-in-ICO since Windows Vista; 'Microsoft recommends that all 32-bit color 256×256 icons in ICO files should be stored in PNG'

Apple Safari Web Content Guide — apple-touch-icon 180×180 (iPhone-Retina) alongside 152/167; device selection rule makes one 180 file cover all iOS devices ('the most appropriate size… is used'); iOS 7+ applies no effects — OS composites the mask (HIG-sourced 'do not pre-round' flagged as quote-unverified)

web.dev maskable icons — important content within the central circle of radius 40% of icon size; opaque background with padding; 'We don't recommend using multiple purposes' — never combine 'any maskable'; ship as a separate manifest entry with purpose 'maskable'
W3C Web Application Manifest spec — 'Icon masks and safe zone': circle with radius 2/5 (40%) of icon size; 'The user agent MUST NOT make any pixel within the safe zone transparent'

Evil Martians 'How to Favicon' (2024 article, updated to the 2026 edition) — community advice (flagged as such): ICO 16+32 from site root, svg + ico both shipped, the exact 4-line head block, sizes='32x32' trick to stop Chrome double-downloading, cruft list (no mask-icon since Safari 12, 'shortcut icon' never valid, Windows tiles no longer required, Coast dead); caniuse link-icon-svg: SVG favicons Chrome 80+/Firefox 41+/Safari 26+ (~91.6%)

Microsoft — 'Declaring Pinned Site Metadata' (archived IE9-era document, msapplication-TileImage/browserconfig.xml); no current Edge/Windows 11 documentation requires it → deprecated-by-default, not generated
